posts.name: Brahma Brews
posts.note: Second Bengaluru microbrewery from the JP Nagar brewpub: a 17,000 sq ft space for 700+ guests with six house beers brewed on site.
body: Beers come off a 10-hectolitre system on site, with a lineup including Belgian Wit, Weizenbock, Mango Ale, the pineapple beer Ananas and Ayurveda, a hibiscus-and-rose brew.
The tropical-styled space has community tables, private booths and semi-open outdoor areas, and the kitchen runs 150+ Indian, Asian, Continental and European dishes.

posts.name: La Verde
posts.note: A new wellness-focused café built around functional drinks, superfoods and everyday café food.
body: The drinks menu centres on hydration, with green juices, electrolyte refreshers and blends made with spirulina, chlorella and supergreens. Signatures include coconut matcha and coconut espresso served in natural coconut shells.
Food covers signature sandwiches, croissant sandwiches, gluten-free almond-flour cakes and seed-and-nut cookies, in a space meant for meeting friends, working remotely or a relaxed meal.

posts.name: Chins Bar, Coffee & Kitchen
posts.note: The team behind Chinlung is opening a 400-seat, three-floor all-day spot that runs from coffee to cocktails and music.
body: The ground floor is a coffee bar built around a Victoria Arduino Eagle One NEO, the first floor is the dining room, and the top floor is the evening bar.

The multi-cuisine menu covers sushi, dim sum, bao, Indian grills, coastal dishes, pizzas and pastas, with picks like Ponzu Butter Dimsum, Mushroom Katsu Bao, Chicken Sukka and Coastal Prawn Curry. It opens 11am to 1am at first, with breakfast and 8am openings after the first month.

posts.name: Bountyful
posts.note: A 40-seat all-vegetarian restaurant drawing on 18 to 20 regional Indian cuisines and home-style cooking.
body: Expect dishes like Hari Moong Dal, Bihari Sattu, Rajasthani Malai Gatta, Bengali Bhapa Paneer and Kashmiri Khatte Nadru, plus a zero-proof drinks list with kokum, jeera and shilajit coolers.
Desserts include Kesar Bhapa Doi, Rose Milk Cake and a Gud Til Chocolate Mousse. It's open 12 to 4pm and 7 to 11pm, closed Mondays.

posts.name: Tossin Pizza
posts.note: The Gurugram-born gourmet pizza brand has opened its first Bengaluru and Karnataka outlet.
body: Founded in 2013 by Chef Rohit Narang and Honey Mehta, Tossin runs 27 outlets across Delhi NCR, Mumbai and Hyderabad. The Koramangala menu brings its veg and non-veg pizzas, pastas, baked dishes and desserts.

posts.name: SMOOR
posts.note: SMOOR's 75th outlet in India, a 48-seat lounge with indoor and outdoor seating, opened as the Bengaluru-born brand turns 10.
body: The 2,450 sq ft ground-floor lounge is aimed at young professionals, corporate customers and residents, open from breakfast through dinner, with coffee and SMOOR's desserts alongside a full menu.

The menu mixes European techniques with Asian flavours: Hoon Twun dumplings, chicken schnitzel, panko fried prawns, a gochujang cottage cheese burger, dandan noodles and teriyaki salmon, plus breakfasts like banana pancakes and kheema pav.

posts.name: bibigo bapsang
posts.note: India's first bibigo bapsang, a Korean quick-service format from GTGO and CJ Foods, built around a build-your-own rice bowl.
body: GTGO, the Korean food company behind GOPIZZA, Gochujang and Dalkomi, has opened the first bibigo bapsang in India at Orion Mall, Rajajinagar, through a partnership with CJ Foods, the company behind the bibigo brand. More Bengaluru outlets are planned by the end of the year.

The signature is BYOB (Build Your Own Bapsang), a customisable bowl inspired by the Korean table with rice, protein and vegetables. The menu also has bibimbap, Korean chicken, Korean fries, corndogs and desserts, at an affordable price point.

posts.name: Roastery Coffee House
posts.note: The coffee chain's newest Bengaluru outlet, called Bengaluru House, with seating for around 80 across about 4,000 sq ft.
body: The design takes subtle cues from Indian arches and traditional design, reworked in a contemporary way. Nearly all the coffee comes from Karnataka, mostly the Chikmagalur region.
The menu runs from cheesy garlic bread, zucchini fries and nachos to a new Hold-in-Hand sandwich range, pastas and flatbread pizzas, with drinks like honey cinnamon, litchi and guava iced coffees.

posts.name: Kebapci
posts.note: Kebapci's third Bengaluru outlet, on 100 Feet Road, built around an open fire grill and its signature Cağ Kebap.
body: Turkish-Mediterranean restaurant Kebapci has opened its third Bengaluru outlet on 100 Feet Road in Indiranagar, following its locations in Koramangala and Forum South and its fine-dining concept Oz at UB City. Founders Aasim Shah and Adeeb Shah said Indiranagar felt long overdue.

The headline dish is the Cağ Kebap, a lamb preparation slow-cooked on a horizontal fire grill and carved tableside, which the brand says it is the only restaurant in India to serve. The new outlet also introduces a Gerçek Adana Kebap, alongside fire-grilled meats, mezze platters and salads.
The interiors were conceptualised by Turkish architects, with the layout bringing guests closer to the open grill.

posts.name: MDP Coffee House
posts.note: A new filter coffee and tea spot on 16th Main, BTM Layout 2nd Stage.
body: MDP Coffee House has opened a new branch in BTM Layout 2nd Stage, serving traditional South Indian filter coffee alongside a range of teas.
It's at #1032, Ground Floor, 16th Main, 16th Cross, BTM Layout 2nd Stage (560076).

posts.name: Friyo
posts.note: Artisanal frozen Greek yogurt and açaí soft-serve bar with in-house bases and a build-your-own toppings bar. About ₹250–450 per person.
body: Friyo is a new frozen Greek yogurt and açaí soft-serve bar in Indiranagar from founders Debasis Das and Subhasmita Panigrahi, built around small-batch, in-house bases rather than premixes.

Classic and chocolate frozen Greek yogurt sit alongside a vegan açaí soft-serve and a Mixed Swirl that combines both. Signature cups include Oops All Biscoff, Just Like Snickers, Cherry on Top and Glow Cup, with a toppings bar of house sauces and crunch mixes.
Desserts are priced about ₹250–450 per person.

posts.name: Kura
posts.note: 3,000 sq ft specialty coffee café with an in-house bakery and a French–Japanese all-day kitchen.
body: Kura, named after the Japanese word for a storehouse of treasured possessions, is a new 3,000 sq ft specialty coffee and all-day dining space in Indiranagar from first-time founders Kiran Vijayakumar and Prajwal Venugopal.

The coffee programme features Indian coffees from the Northeast, Himalayan foothills, Koraput, Araku and the Western Ghats alongside international roasters, with milk-clarified coffees, Frost blended cold brew and three-beverage coffee journeys.
The kitchen pairs French technique with Japanese precision: house-laminated viennoiserie, pastries and hand-rolled pasta, plus Eggs Benedict, seafood and New Zealand lamb rack on the all-day menu.

posts.name: Bahati
posts.note: RJ-DJ Rohit Barker's two-floor sky club with house, Latin and Afro sets.
body: Bahati, Swahili for 'good luck', is RJ and DJ Rohit Barker's newest venture, taking over the 17th and 18th floors of a building on Kasturba Road with views over the Cubbon Park canopy, Kingfisher Tower and Chinnaswamy Stadium.

The name comes from a blue-eyed leopard Barker and his partners spotted in the Masai Mara. The 17th floor is a low-seated lounge with soft lighting; the upper deck has the dance floor and DJ console. The music leans house, Latin and Afro, with Barker and Nikhil Chinapa on the decks for the opening weekend.

Cocktails follow the wild theme: Chui (leopard) mixes reposado tequila, mezcal, charred pineapple and Kanthari chillies, and Maridadi (elegant) pairs Scotch with coconut, rooibos and pandan. Cost for two is about ₹5,000.

posts.name: Beanlore
posts.note: Fourth outlet of the in-house-roasting café, set in a two-floor old Bangalore bungalow.

posts.name: Foo
posts.note: Fourth Bengaluru Foo: 97 covers, 100+ Pan-Asian tapas, a central bar and an outdoor pergola.

posts.name: BLR Brewing Co.
posts.note: Seventh outlet of the homegrown brewpub. About ₹2,000 for two.

posts.name: Druma
posts.note: 60-cover contemporary vegetarian restaurant mixing Indian, South Indian, Pan-Asian and global plates. About ₹2,200 for two.
body: Druma is a 2,100 sq ft, 60-cover vegetarian restaurant at the Cosmopolitan Club in Jayanagar 4th Block, built around the idea of 'humble dining' with a design drawn from Kannada culture and South Indian architecture.
Signature plates include a Mushroom Cappuccino with khari, Samosa Mille Feuille Chaat, Pesto Kunafa Tofu and a Chettinad Paneer Quesadilla made with Malabar parotta. It's open 12:30 pm to midnight.

posts.name: Alpaca
posts.note: India's first dedicated chocolate drinks house: eight cacao intensities, hot or iced, with milk and topping options.

posts.name: Goonj
posts.note: A 75-seat Indian bar and restaurant on 100 Feet Road built around lesser-seen Indian recipes and a contemporary cocktail programme.
body: Spread across 2,500 sq ft on the fourth floor, Goonj looks at Indian food through the lens of memory, drawing on family kitchens, festive meals and old cooking techniques.
Dishes include Dal Bukhara and Bhutte Ka Kees, alongside cocktails inspired by Indian flavours. Price for two is about ₹2,700.

posts.name: Baci Baci Osteria
posts.note: A new Italian spot serving wood-fired pizzas, handmade pasta and Italian coffees in cosy, old-world interiors.
body: The space is meant for relaxed meals with friends, open from noon to midnight, with a price for two of about ₹1,600.

posts.name: Dindigul Thalappakatti
posts.note: New Koramangala outlet of the Dindigul biryani brand, inaugurated by Kannada actor Shivarajkumar.

posts.name: Toast House
posts.note: Bread-first café built around house-made shokupan sandos and French toast.

posts.name: Subko × The Humming Tree
posts.note: Full-scale Subko café with a bakehouse and cacao, inside The Humming Tree.

posts.name: The Filter Coffee
posts.note: First airport outlet: filter coffee and South Indian favourites, 24 hours, with Travel Food Services.

posts.name: Oye Kake
posts.note: Second Bengaluru outlet, adding a live lassi bar for the first time.
